EXECUTIVE SUMMARY
Tensions in the Middle East have reached an extreme level, with multiple US media outlets reporting that President Trump has ordered a new, potentially multi-day attack on Iranian energy infrastructure and military sites, which could commence as early as this weekend. Simultaneously, US Embassies across the region have issued urgent security alerts advising American citizens to consider immediate departure, while Iran has threatened "Stone Age" retaliation against regional infrastructure, including Israeli and US energy assets.

IRAN
Military operations in and against Iran are at an unprecedented level of anticipation. Multiple US media outlets (Wall Street Journal, ABC, NBC, CNN, CBS) report that President Trump has ordered a new attack on Iran, with targets potentially including energy infrastructure (power plants, refineries), missile sites, and nuclear facilities. These strikes could begin as early as this weekend, 03 August 2026, and last for several days, with discussions about concluding operations before financial markets open on Monday. A US CENTCOM official is reported to have drafted a plan for an extensive two-week bombing campaign. Conversely, a senior Israeli official stated Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations or join any military actions against Iran. The New York Times reported a past US strike on a residential home in Qeshm, Iran, using a 2,000-pound Mark-84 bomb, killed three people, including a two-year-old child.

Iran has issued severe warnings of retaliation. Ebrahim Rezaei, a member of Iran's Parliament National Security Commission, stated that if Iran is attacked, it will return the entire region and its infrastructure to the "Stone Age." Major General Abdollahi, Commander of Iran’s Khatam al-Anbiya Central Headquarters, warned that the US is pursuing widespread regional war and any country shielding the US "will burn in the fire of war." The Tasnim news agency cited a senior security official stating Iran has prepared a "broad response" targeting critical Israeli infrastructure and US energy assets in the region. Iran's Fars News Agency published a list of energy sites in Saudi Arabia, UAE, Qatar, Kuwait, Bahrain, and Israel's Tamar and Leviathan gas fields as being within range of Iranian missiles. The IRGC Navy has reportedly issued warnings to vessels in the Strait of Hormuz, causing several tankers to alter course.

Iran's military also reportedly conducted a drone attack on Kuwait, targeting a government facility in northern Kuwait and civilian assets on Bubiyan Island, causing property damage, with Kuwaiti air defenses intercepting incoming missiles. Unverified reports also claim two oil tankers were struck in the Makran Sea today, and another this morning. A reported explosion in Islamabad-e-Gharb, Kermanshah province, western Iran, was officially attributed to an old shell from the Iran-Iraq War detonating due to heat, though some unverified sources suggest a failed drone attack. A new billboard in Vali Asr Square, Tehran, displays the slogan "Ya Latharat al-Hussein" (Call for Vengeance), signaling defiance. Iran's security chief, Mohammad-Baqer Zolkadr, warned that continued US naval blockade would strengthen the closure of the Strait of Hormuz and other strategic chokepoints.

Internally, there are reports of significant concerns and preparations. Ali Khazrian, a Tehran MP, suggested building underground "governance cities" to protect officials during an invasion. Unverified reports claim evacuations are underway at Shahid Rajaee Port in Bandar Abbas, Dezful's Vahdati Airbase, and Mehrabad Airport in Tehran, with tank movements reported towards border areas near Ahvaz-Abadan. These claims are officially denied by Hormozgan province officials. Employees in the electricity and petrochemical sectors have been warned to avoid work in the coming week. There are also allegations that all data centers are on alert to cut internet access in case of war. Russia is reportedly providing Iran with satellite surveillance and signals intelligence.

ISRAEL
Israeli military operations continue in Gaza and along the Lebanese border. An Israeli officer was moderately injured during "operational activity" in southern Lebanon overnight. In Gaza, the IDF and Shin Bet killed Abd al-Rahim Abd al-Hay Youssef Kardi, a deputy Hamas cell commander and doctor at Shifa Hospital, in an airstrike in Gaza City. Kardi was involved in the October 7 massacre, holding Israeli hostage Romi Gonen, and the body of Cpl. Noa Marciano. The IDF stated he was planning attacks on troops and Israeli civilians.

Politically, a source reiterated Israel's stance that there will be no IDF withdrawal from the current yellow line in Gaza without a true disarmament of Hamas. US President Trump claimed Israel is "very happy" with the current agreement in Gaza. Trump also admitted that Secretary of State Marco Rubio's anti-ICC campaign was intended to shield Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu from international prosecution. US EUCOM Commander, General Alexus Grynkewich, warned the Pentagon that he lacks enough naval forces to continue defending Israel from Iranian ballistic missile attacks, possibly forcing him to prioritize US homeland defense. Netanyahu reportedly blocked the transfer of Iron Dome batteries to Ukraine.

GAZA & WEST BANK
Israeli forces killed Abd al-Rahim Abd al-Hay Youssef Kardi, a Hamas deputy cell commander, in a Gaza City airstrike. Kardi was implicated in the October 7 massacre and the captivity of Israeli hostage Romi Gonen and the body of Cpl. Noa Marciano. An Israeli drone strike in Sheikh Radwan, Gaza City, killed at least one Palestinian and critically injured another. A medicine storage warehouse at Al-Aqsa Martyrs Hospital in central Gaza was destroyed in an Israeli strike, displacing dozens of families. The Ministry of Health in Gaza reported that over half of medicines are out of stock due to the Israeli blockade, and 28% of diseases are linked to contaminated water.

Hamas has stated that it will only discuss its weapons after an Israeli withdrawal from Gaza, an end to aggression, reconstruction efforts, and guarantees for Palestinian statehood. A political source reaffirmed Israel's position that there would be no IDF withdrawal from the current yellow line in Gaza without a genuine disarmament of Hamas.

In the West Bank, Israeli forces demolished a 120-year-old building and Palestinian water wells in the northern Jordan Valley. Online instigation reportedly led to new settler raids south of Nablus. A settler was documented opening live fire on a 9-year-old child in Al-Mughayyir, east of Ramallah. The humanitarian situation in Khan Yunis remains dire, with displaced Gaza residents enduring scorching heat in tents.

LEBANON
An Israeli officer was moderately injured during "operational activity" in southern Lebanon overnight. The specific circumstances of the incident were not immediately published by the IDF. Israeli forces have reportedly intensified assaults on Lebanon, striking southern Lebanon. Hezbollah condemned alleged Israeli explosions beneath Beaufort Castle and continued aggression in southern Lebanon, urging Lebanese authorities to support self-defense rights for people in the south. Al-Hadath reported that a new round of negotiations between Lebanon and Israel will commence in Rome on Tuesday for three days, where Lebanon plans to propose moving to Phase Two "test areas," including Bint Jbeil or Al-Khiyam, and will not accept Israeli verification of Phase One implementation.

SYRIA & IRAQ
The US military began and is nearing completion of withdrawing all its forces and Patriot missile batteries from the base in Erbil, northern Iraq. Fire broke out at a fuel storage facility at the Shamak refinery in southwest Erbil, halting its operations. US aircraft were observed flying over northern Iraq, including the Nineveh plains. Funeral ceremonies were held in Nineveh for martyrs killed in alleged US-Saudi attacks in Iraq. The Iraqi Oil Ministry announced a trilateral agreement with Turkey to resume oil exports via the Ceyhan pipeline with a capacity of 750,000 barrels per day. Turkey is reportedly pressuring Iran to cease drone attacks on Iranian-Kurdish opposition groups in northern Iraq, fearing that continued attacks could push the Kurds closer to Israel and jeopardize Turkey's peace deal with the PKK. Israeli forces expanded illegal incursions into Syria's Quneitra province.

GULF STATES
Kuwait's military reported that Iranian drone attacks targeted several vital facilities in Kuwait, including a government facility in the north and civilian assets on Bubiyan Island, causing property damage. Kuwaiti air defenses intercepted Iranian missiles.

Saudi Arabia, along with 13 other nations including Pakistan, Turkey, Egypt, Jordan, Yemen, Bangladesh, Nigeria, Sudan, Djibouti, and Somalia, announced the formation of a multinational maritime defense coalition aimed at securing the Red Sea, Bab el-Mandeb, and the Gulf of Aden. The coalition's headquarters will be in Saudi Arabia. Houthi forces claimed eight Saudi oil tankers were forced to change course towards the Cape of Good Hope due to a naval blockade on Saudi oil shipping. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister, Faisal bin Farhan, discussed the importance of diplomatic efforts to reduce regional tensions with his Turkish counterpart, Hakan Fidan. There are unconfirmed reports that Saudi Arabia is planning a heavy military offensive against Houthi militias in Yemen. Bahrain International Airport issued cautionary alerts for travelers and staff.

A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile approximately 20km northeast of Oman in the southern route of the Strait of Hormuz, resulting in damage to its engine room and the vessel losing command. Satellite imagery identified a US Nimitz-class aircraft carrier (USS Abraham Lincoln or USS George H.W. Bush) sailing south in the Arabian Sea, east of Oman. Iran's security chief warned that continued US "warmongering" would lead to a tighter closure of the Strait of Hormuz and other strategic waterways.

KEY DEVELOPMENTS
1.  **Imminent US-Israeli Strikes on Iran:** Multiple US media outlets (WSJ, ABC, NBC, CNN, CBS) report President Trump ordered a new attack on Iranian energy infrastructure and military sites, potentially beginning this weekend (03 August 2026) and lasting several days.
2.  **Widespread US Embassy Security Warnings:** US Embassies across the Middle East, including Israel, Saudi Arabia, UAE, Kuwait, Qatar, Oman, Bahrain, Egypt, Jordan, and Iraq, issued alerts advising citizens to consider departing the region or be prepared for immediate exit due to escalating tensions.
3.  **Iranian Threats of Regional Retaliation:** Iranian officials threatened to return the entire region to the "Stone Age" and target critical Israeli infrastructure and US energy assets in response to any attack.
4.  **Iranian Drone/Missile Attack on Kuwait:** Kuwait's military reported Iranian drone attacks on vital facilities, including a government site in northern Kuwait and assets on Bubiyan Island, causing damage, with Kuwaiti air defenses intercepting missiles.
5.  **US Military Naval Force Concerns:** US EUCOM Commander, Gen. Alexus Grynkewich, warned the Pentagon he lacks sufficient naval destroyers to defend Israel from Iranian ballistic missiles while meeting US homeland defense needs.
6.  **Tanker Attack off Oman:** A tanker was struck by an unknown projectile approximately 20km northeast of Oman, damaging its engine room and leaving it not under command.
7.  **US Military Withdrawal from Erbil:** The US military is nearing completion of withdrawing all forces and Patriot missile batteries from its base in Erbil, northern Iraq.
8.  **Hamas Commander Killed in Gaza:** The IDF and Shin Bet killed Abd al-Rahim Abd al-Hay Youssef Kardi, a deputy Hamas cell commander involved in the October 7 massacre and holding Israeli hostages, in a Gaza City airstrike.

THREAT ASSESSMENT
The risk of escalation is extreme, with imminent threats of US-Israeli military strikes against Iran and explicit Iranian warnings of severe regional retaliation, including against Israeli and Gulf State infrastructure. Active flashpoints include the direct Iran-US/Israel conflict, the Strait of Hormuz and Red Sea (where a tanker was recently attacked and Houthi blockades persist), and the Lebanon-Israel border following an IDF officer injury and ongoing Israeli strikes. Military postures are shifting rapidly, with the US planning significant offensive actions while simultaneously facing reported naval asset limitations, and the US withdrawal from Erbil suggests a strategic repositioning. Iran is on high alert, with reported internal preparations and explicit threats of immediate and widespread counter-attacks. Red lines appear to be a direct attack on Iranian territory or critical infrastructure, which Iran has stated will trigger an immediate and devastating regional response.

REGIONAL & INTERNATIONAL RESPONSE
The **US** posture indicates a move towards decisive military action, with President Trump having reportedly ordered new attacks on Iran aimed at forcing "surrender" and ending Iran's nuclear program and control over Hormuz. The White House affirmed that Iran would not possess nuclear weapons under Trump's presidency. US Embassies across the Middle East issued urgent security advisories for their citizens to consider departing the region.

**Gulf States** are reacting to the heightened tensions. Kuwait reported a direct Iranian drone and missile attack. Saudi Arabia has initiated a 14-nation multinational maritime defense coalition to secure vital waterways like the Red Sea and Bab el-Mandeb, and there are reports of Saudi plans for a heavy military offensive against Houthi militias. Saudi Arabia's Foreign Minister discussed de-escalation with Turkey.

**EU members** have expressed concern over regional stability. The EU Naval Force "Aspides" successfully escorted a merchant ship through the Red Sea. Internally, the EU is grappling with a significant migrant crisis in Spain's Ceuta enclave, leading to Italy temporarily suspending its Schengen agreement with Spain and calls from 22 EU leaders for stricter migration controls and potential temporary border checks within Schengen.

**Russia** is actively engaged in the conflict in Ukraine, with Kiev experiencing major missile and drone attacks, including a recent barrage of 35 missiles and 185 drones. Ukraine's President Zelensky noted a critical shortage of Patriot interceptor missiles. Russia is also reportedly assisting Iran by providing satellite surveillance and signals intelligence.

**China** has criticized US actions, condemning the addition of Chinese companies to the US forced labor list as "economic coercion." China also announced joint naval and air exercises in the disputed Scarborough Shoal area of the South China Sea.

**Turkey** signed a one-year agreement with Iraq for the Ceyhan oil pipeline. Turkey is also reportedly pressuring Iran to halt drone attacks on Iranian-Kurdish opposition groups in northern Iraq, concerned about regional stability and potential impacts on its own peace deal with the PKK. Turkish President Erdogan stated that Turkey's security extends to Aleppo, Damascus, and Beirut, indicating an assertive regional foreign policy.

INTELLIGENCE NOTES
Several unverified claims and contradictions exist within the provided intelligence. A senior Israeli official's statement that "Israel is unaware of a decision to restart full military operations" directly contradicts multiple US media reports of US-Israeli planning and coordination for imminent strikes against Iran, creating ambiguity regarding the extent of Israel's direct involvement. The reported explosion near Islamabad-e-Gharb was initially presented as an attack by some Iranian sources, but later officially attributed to an old shell detonation, while unverified channels continue to suggest a drone strike.

Internal Iranian reports of military movements and evacuations in southern provinces (Bandar Abbas, Dezful, Ahvaz-Abadan) and Tehran's Mehrabad Airport are contradicted by official Iranian statements denying any evacuation orders and affirming normal conditions, indicating potential information operations or fear-mongering. President Trump's detailed claims at Camp David about the "destruction" of Iran's navy and air defenses and his vivid description of missile interceptions ("bing, bing, bing") lack independent corroboration and appear to be part of a broader psychological and political messaging strategy. Iran's threats of "Stone Age" retaliation are also highly hyperbolic, designed to deter. The CENTCOM denial of the Strait of Hormuz closure directly refutes Iranian rhetoric of impending closure. There is a reporting gap regarding the specific nature of the "operational activity" in southern Lebanon that injured an IDF officer, as well as precise details on the tanker attack off Oman. The alleged Russian provision of intelligence to Iran lacks confirmation from either Iranian or Russian sources in this feed.
